title: Destabilization of TIP60-PXR complex by rifampicin impairs wound-induced cell migration.
journal: The Journal of pharmacology and experimental therapeutics
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子对接与MD模拟研究利福平对TIP60-PXR转录因子复合物稳定性的破坏，属蛋白-蛋白互作而非TF-DNA结合，但方法可迁移至TF-DNA界面建模。
abstract: The Tat interactive protein 60 (TIP60)-pregnane and xenobiotic receptor (PXR) complex plays a pivotal role in regulating cell migration during wound healing, and disruption of this complex can impair this function. Because PXR is a ligand-activated transcription factor responsive to structurally diverse compounds, we investigated how different ligands can influence the structural and functional integrity of the TIP60-PXR complex. Using an integrated computational approach, we assessed how various PXR ligands affect complex stability and among them, rifampicin, an established PXR activator, emerged as a notable disruptor. Although most ligands exhibited comparable docking energies in both PXR alone and the TIP60-PXR complex, rifampicin showed a significantly higher binding energy when docked with the complex, suggesting destabilization. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that rifampicin disrupts key interface residues, with significant root mean square deviation fluctuations and a failure to stabilize the complex. Molecular mechanics Poisson-Boltzmann surface area binding free energy calculations further confirmed rifampicin's destabilizing effect. To validate these findings in a cellular context, we conducted live-cell imaging and coimmunoprecipitation assays. Rifampicin treatment drastically reduced the intracellular colocalization and physical interaction between TIP60 and PXR, thereby significantly compromising their ability to support wound-induced cell migration. This was evident across multiple cell lines, correlating with PXR expression levels. Our findings establish a direct mechanistic link between ligand-induced structural changes in PXR and the functional impairment of the TIP60-PXR complex. This study provides a critical platform for understanding how small molecules modulate coregulator interactions and offers new insights for designing targeted therapeutics aimed at enhancing tissue repair. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study identifies ligand-dependent disruption of the TIP60-pregnane and xenobiotic receptor (PXR) complex as a critical regulatory mechanism controlling wound-induced cell migration. By combining computational modeling with cellular validation, it reveals that rifampicin uniquely destabilizes the TIP60-PXR interaction despite being a known PXR activator. These findings uncover how small molecules can selectively modulate coregulator complexes, linking ligand-induced structural changes to impaired tissue repair. The work provides mechanistic insight with important implications for drug safety and regenerative therapeutic design.
abstract_zh: Tat交互蛋白60（TIP60）-孕烷X受体（PXR）复合物在伤口愈合过程中调控细胞迁移中发挥关键作用，而该复合物的破坏可损害此功能。由于PXR是一种配体激活的转录因子，对结构多样的化合物有响应，我们研究了不同配体如何影响TIP60-PXR复合物的结构和功能完整性。采用综合计算方法，我们评估了多种PXR配体对复合物稳定性的影响，其中，利福平（一种公认的PXR激活剂）作为显著破坏者脱颖而出。尽管大多数配体在单独PXR和TIP60-PXR复合物中表现出相当的对接能量，但利福平在与复合物对接时显示出显著更高的结合能，提示其具有去稳定化作用。分子动力学模拟揭示，利福平破坏关键界面残基，伴随显著的均方根偏差波动，且未能稳定复合物。分子力学泊松-玻尔兹曼表面积结合自由能计算进一步证实了利福平的去稳定化效应。为在细胞环境中验证这些发现，我们进行了活细胞成像和共免疫沉淀实验。利福平处理显著降低了TIP60与PXR之间的细胞内共定位和物理相互作用，从而严重损害了它们支持伤口诱导细胞迁移的能力。这在多种细胞系中均明显，并与PXR表达水平相关。我们的发现建立了配体诱导的PXR结构变化与TIP60-PXR复合物功能损伤之间的直接机制联系。本研究为理解小分子如何调节共调节因子相互作用提供了关键平台，并为设计旨在增强组织修复的靶向治疗提供了新见解。意义声明：本研究将配体依赖性TIP60-孕烷X受体（PXR）复合物破坏确定为控制伤口诱导细胞迁移的关键调控机制。通过结合计算建模与细胞验证，它揭示利福平尽管是已知的PXR激活剂，却独特地使TIP60-PXR相互作用去稳定化。这些发现揭示了小分子如何选择性调节共调节因子复合物，将配体诱导的结构变化与组织修复受损联系起来。该工作提供了机制性见解，对药物安全性和再生治疗设计具有重要意义。
